sn12.13:1.2: The terms “ascetics and brahmins” is often used as a generic catch-all for ‘religious practitioners” ([sn3.1:2.1]()). Technically, “ascetics” (_samaṇa_) include the renunciate practitioners of the non-Vedic religions such as the Buddhists, Jains, and Ājīvakas. These sometimes affiliated, sometimes squabbling religious movements typically rejected Vedic authority and caste system, and proposed their own philosophy and practice ([dn2:2.2]()). “Brahmins” were a hereditary caste of Vedic priests charged with maintaining Vedic scripture and performing rituals. In the Vedas, brahmins served worldly prosperity and, more vaguely, heavenly rebirth. Perhaps under the influence of the ascetics, they later developed a renunciate movement of contemplatives who looked for a merger with Divinity beyond the cycle of rebirth.
